Complete models, each on a page of its own with the same parts: what the model is and why a modeler would build it this way, its state-transition diagram, its parameters, the code, a result with a plot, and where to go next. They cover a range of diseases and structures, rather than building one model up step by step as the [tutorials](tutorials.qmd) do. Each page runs as it is.

## Short examples

Each of these is one model and one result, and runs in seconds.

| Model | What it shows |
|---|---|
| [SIR, four ways](gallery/sir.qmd) | The four ways of writing a model, which give the same model; the same model as an ODE, two kinds of stochastic model, and agents |
| [SEIR with a realistic infectious period](gallery/seir_erlang.qmd) | A latent period; an infectious period with Erlang stages against an exponential one |
| [Hospitalization and death](gallery/hospitalization.qmd) | A split on entry (who goes to hospital) and competing hazards (death or discharge); severity by age as a Python function, run as compartments and as agents |
| [Cholera with a water reservoir](gallery/cholera.qmd) | A state that is not people (bacteria in the water), with flows in from and out to outside the model |
| [Age groups and contacts](gallery/age_contacts.qmd) | An age-stratified SIR with a contact matrix; the United Kingdom's population with contacts by setting, and a school closure that removes one setting |
| [Vaccination as a stratification](gallery/vaccination_strata.qmd) | Vaccinated and unvaccinated groups, and a campaign that moves people between them |
| [Cases, hospitalizations, and deaths, fitted to data](gallery/outcomes_fit.qmd) | Outcomes with delays; data made from the model; fitting β with `sim.fit()` |
| [An STI on a sexual network](gallery/sexual_network.qmd) | Transmission per sex act over partnerships; many runs as agents |

## Case studies

Longer pages, each with more than one model or many runs.

| Model | What it shows |
|---|---|
| [Checks against theory](gallery/theory_checks.qmd) | The final size against the Kermack–McKendrick equation, as an ODE; the chance of a major outbreak against 1 − 1/R0, with 1,500 stochastic runs |
| [Measles in London, three ways](gallery/measles_london.qmd) | He et al. (2010)'s stochastic measles model with school terms and cohort entry: declared with a little code, written as code, and declared with noise; a likelihood of its own, a compiled loop, and a particle filter at the published parameters. About a minute to run |
| [Beyond disease](gallery/beyond_disease.qmd) | Agent-based models with no disease: wealth that becomes unequal, and birds that flock, with an animation |

## Models from other frameworks

Each framework that Starsim can [import from](user_guide/building_import.qmd), from Atomica and EpiModel to odin and summer2, has a page in the [Lingua Franca](https://starsim.org/lingua_franca/) docs with a showcase model written in that framework and in Starsim, and how their results and run times compare; [Comparison with other frameworks](https://starsim.org/lingua_franca/models/comparison.html) lists them all.

## Library modules

The Starsim [library](user_guide/library_index.qmd) (`import starsim.library as ssl`) has more examples: diseases (HIV, cholera, malaria, TB, and others), networks (households, space, and theoretical networks), maternal-child health, and health economics. They are illustrative rather than validated, and meant to be copied and adapted.

## Scripts in the repository

A few longer examples are kept as scripts in the [`docs/examples`](https://github.com/starsimhub/starsim/tree/main/docs/examples) folder of the repository, to read and adapt:

- **An embedding network** ([`networks/embedding.py`](https://github.com/starsimhub/starsim/blob/main/docs/examples/networks/embedding.py)): pairs people by their closeness in a continuous space of traits.
- **One model in several languages** ([`translations/`](https://github.com/starsimhub/starsim/tree/main/docs/examples/translations)): the same simple SIS model written in plain Python, Numba, JAX, Julia, and Rust, next to the Starsim version, for comparing their speed.
- **LASER** ([`laser/`](https://github.com/starsimhub/starsim/tree/main/docs/examples/laser)): a LASER example and its Starsim equivalents, with scripts to time them.
